blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
We present VGM-VS, a visual servoing method built on a pretrained feed-forward
visual geometry model. Given the current view and a reference image captured at
the target configuration, we estimate the relative camera pose with a visual geometry model and apply it iteratively as the pose increment of a closed-loop pose-based visual servoing (PBVS) scheme. The geometry-aware representation acquired from large-scale pretraining keeps this estimate reliable when the target is occluded, weakly textured, or covers only a small part of the image. However, the scale ambiguity inherent to these models leaves the predicted translation defined up to an unknown scale, while the pose increment must be metric for robot control. We close this gap with a scene-specific metric adaptation: the robot autonomously records image–pose pairs along a predefined motion starting from the target pose, and we fine-tune the camera head on these data, jointly learning the hand–eye transform and thus removing the need for a dedicated calibration process. We evaluate our method on three real-world assembly tasks with demanding tolerances: USB-C cable picking, cable insertion, and RAM insertion. Running in real time at 30Hz, VGM-VS converges to submillimeter terminal accuracy on the cable tasks, and reaches success rates of 90–100% when the target is moved during servoing. It converges in all trials under initial displacements of up to 30cm from the reference pose and with 50% of the target object occluded, outperforming the compared visual servoing baselines.

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en: High-precision assembly remains one of the most demanding problems in industrial robotics, as it requires aligning parts within submillimeter tolerances. Achieving such an alignment from vision is difficult: the gripper partially occludes the assembly interface, the surfaces are weakly textured and specular, and the interface itself covers only a few pixels of the image. A pose estimate acquired before the approach may be insufficient to complete the alignment. Visual feedback can correct the remaining displacement, but obtaining reliable feedback becomes challenging when the target itself is poorly observed.
blocks.zh: 高精度组装仍然是工业机器人中最有要求的问题之一,因为它需要将部分配合到亚毫米耐受度内. 从视觉中实现这样的对齐是困难的:抓子部分占据了组装接口,表面的纹理和光谱都很弱,界面本身只覆盖图像的几个像素. 在采用这种方法之前获得的假设估计可能不足以完成调整。 视觉反馈可以纠正剩余的流离失所现象,但当目标本身没有得到充分的观察时,获得可靠的反馈就变得具有挑战性.

blocks.en:
Visual servoing controls robot motion by regulating image features or estimated poses relative to a desired configuration [ 1 , 2 ] . Object pose estimation instead aligns the robot with an explicit estimate of the target pose [ 3 ] , a paradigm that still inherits the visibility limits described above. In contrast, scene-feature [ 4 , 5 ] and direct [ 6 , 7 ] methods regress motion from whatever the image contains. This broader visual context is useful in structured assembly cells: when a target remains fixed relative to its surroundings, the visible workspace structure can anchor a reference even when the target is partially occluded. Existing scene-based methods, however, reach only millimeter- to centimeter-level
accuracy or suffer from a small convergence basin, leaving open whether scene structure
can support the submillimeter accuracy that precise assembly demands.

blocks.en:
Feed-forward visual geometry models offer a promising basis for this task. DUSt3R [ 8 ] and Mast3R [ 9 ] regress pointmaps from image pairs, and VGGT [ 10 ] and VGGT- Ω \Omega [ 11 ] extend this to many views and additionally predict camera poses, in a single forward pass without per-scene optimization. These models regress camera motion from the
whole image rather than from the target alone, featuring
scene anchoring in exactly the sense required above. Their accuracy, however, is characterized only up to scale: reconstruction is evaluated after alignment to the ground truth, and relative-pose benchmarks score translation by direction, so neither establishes whether a predicted translation is millimeter-level accurate. Visual servoing instead requires both the direction of the remaining motion and its magnitude in physical units, and a scale that varies between frames makes a small stopping threshold impossible to apply. Closing this gap requires adapting the pretrained representation so that its translations become metric within the deployment workspace.

blocks.en: We present VGM-VS, a visual servoing framework that combines scene-anchored relative localization with scene-specific metric adaptation, as illustrated in Fig. . Given a current image and a reference image captured at the desired task configuration, VGM-VS estimates the relative camera pose from the surrounding scene structure, without an explicit estimate of the object pose. With the camera rigidly mounted on the robot end-effector, this estimate becomes the increment of a closed-loop controller, in which each new observation refines the previous command. To make the predicted translation metric, we fine-tune the camera head on data that the robot records autonomously in the scene. We evaluate VGM-VS on three real-world assembly tasks requiring precise positioning: USB-C cable picking, cable insertion, and RAM insertion, where it reaches submillimeter terminal accuracy on the cable tasks and tolerates large initial displacements, partial occlusions, and objects displaced during servoing.

blocks.en:
Our contributions are summarized as follows: • Scene-anchored visual servoing. A closed-loop frame-
work that uses static workspace geometry rather than
object models to servo to a reference image. Relative poses from a feed-forward visual geometry model guide iterative corrections, reducing the reliance on single-shot pose accuracy. • Scene-specific metric adaptation. A procedure that fine-tunes the camera head on autonomously collected data while freezing the pretrained backbone, recovering metric pose predictions and the hand–eye transform without a dedicated calibration. • Real-robot validation. An evaluation on three high-precision assembly tasks under large initial displacements, partial occlusions, and dynamic scene changes, showing lower terminal pose error and higher success rates than classical and learning-based baselines.

blocks.en: II Related Work
blocks.zh: 二. 相关工作

blocks.en: II-A Visual Servoing
blocks.zh: II-A 视觉破坏

blocks.en: Classical visual servoing is divided into image-based visual servoing (IBVS), which minimizes feature errors in the image plane, and position-based visual servoing (PBVS), which minimizes a reconstructed pose error [ 12 , 1 , 2 ] ; hybrid 2 1/2-D schemes [ 13 ] trade off between the local stability of IBVS and the dependence of PBVS on accurate pose estimation, calibration, and object models. Both families typically rely on sparse hand-crafted features such as SIFT [ 14 ] , ORB [ 15 ] , or AKAZE [ 16 ] , so precision degrades under weak texture, illumination changes, and occlusion, while direct photometric servoing [ 6 , 7 ] avoids feature extraction altogether at the cost of a small convergence basin.
blocks.zh: 古典视觉伺服分为基于图像的视觉伺服器(IBVS),将图像平面中的特征误差最小化;基于位置的视觉伺服器(PBVS),将重建的姿势误差最小化[12,1,2];混合2 1/2-D方案[13]在IBVS的局部稳定性和PBVS对准确的姿势估计,校准,以及对象模型的依赖之间进行交换. 这两种家庭一般都依靠手工业的稀少特征,如SIFT[14],ORB[15],或AKAZE[16],因此精度在纹理薄弱、照明变化和隔离下降解,而直接的光度测量伺服[6,7]则以小的汇合盆地为代价完全避免了特征提取.

blocks.en: Learning-based methods relax these assumptions. Early works regress the relative camera pose with CNNs inside a PBVS loop [ 17 , 18 ] , reaching submillimeter accuracy with Siamese networks in scene-specific settings [ 19 ] , while others servo on learned representations such as optical flow [ 20 , 21 ] , keypoints [ 22 , 23 ] , or autoencoder and SE(3)-equivariant latent spaces [ 24 , 25 ] . CNS [ 26 ] encodes keypoint correspondences into a graph and trains a GNN controller purely in simulation, attaining submillimeter precision with a large convergence basin, and CNSv2 [ 27 ] extends it to textureless scenes via probabilistic matching. ViT-VS [ 4 ] and ART-VS [ 5 ] instead exploit pretrained Vision Transformer features within a classical IBVS loop, thereby generalizing without task-specific training. Still, existing pipelines either inherit the local stability and Jacobian conditioning issues of IBVS, or rely on pose estimators that lack a metric, geometry-grounded scene representation, limiting the achievable precision and robustness trade-off.
blocks.zh: 基于学习的方法放松了这些假设. 早期的作品将CNN在PBVS环 [17,18] 内的相对相机姿势倒置,在场景特定环境下与暹罗网络达到亚毫米计精确度[19],而其他在光学流[20,21],键点[22,23]等学得的表示上的伺服器,或自动编码器和SE(3)-等效潜伏空间[24,25]. CNS [26] 将键点对应编码成图表,并训练一个GNN控制器,纯粹在模拟中实现亚毫米计精确度与一个大趋同盆地,CNSv2 [27]通过概率匹配将其扩展到无纹理场景. VIT-VS [4] 和 ART-VS [5] 转而在一个经典的IBVS循环中利用预先训练过的Vision Transformer特性,从而在没有任务特定训练的情况下概括化. 尽管如此,现有的管道要么继承了IBVS的地方稳定性和雅各布置问题,要么依赖缺乏量度,几何定位的场景表现,限制了可实现的精确性和稳健性权衡.

blocks.en: II-B Visual Geometry Models
blocks.zh: II-B 视觉几何模型

blocks.en: Feed-forward visual geometry models replace multi-stage reconstruction pipelines with a single network. DUSt3R [ 8 ] regresses dense pointmaps from uncalibrated image pairs, jointly encoding geometry, correspondence, and relative pose; MASt3R [ 9 ] adds metric-scale outputs and dense descriptors, and follow-ups extend the paradigm to multi-view, streaming, and dynamic settings [ 28 , 29 ] . VGGT [ 10 ] unifies this family in one transformer that predicts cameras, depth, pointmaps, and point tracks for hundreds of views, π 3 \pi^{3} [ 30 ] removes reference-view bias through permutation equivariance, and MapAnything [ 31 ] handles heterogeneous input–output modalities at the metric scale. Most recently, VGGT- Ω \Omega [ 11 ] shows that reconstruction quality scales predictably with model and data size, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy on static and dynamic scenes.
blocks.zh: Feed-forward视觉几何模型用单一网络取代多阶段重建管道. DUST3R [8] 将密点图从未校准的图像对返回到密点图,联合编码几何,函证和相对姿势; MASt3R [9] 增加了度量输出和密点描述符,后续将范式扩展到多视图、流线和动态设置 [28, 29] 。 VGGT [10] 将这个家族统一在一个变压器中,用于预测摄像头、深度、尖点图和成百上千个视图的指向轨道, XXX 3\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ 最近,VGGT-ship – ship \Omega [11] 显示重建质量尺度可以预测到模型和数据大小,在静态和动态场景上实现最先进的精度.

blocks.en: In robotics, these models serve as geometry-aware encoders for imitation policies [ 32 , 33 ] , spatial-token providers for Vision Language Action (VLA) models [ 34 ] , and front-ends for SLAM and relocalization [ 35 , 36 ] . Yet they are evaluated almost exclusively on reconstruction and localization benchmarks where centimeter errors are tolerable. Whether such models can deliver the submillimeter, sub-degree accuracy demanded by closed-loop servoing remains open. VGM-VS addresses this gap by revisiting their geometric outputs as a metric feedback signal for high-precision servoing, benchmarked against classical IBVS [ 1 ] and feature-driven ART-VS [ 5 ] .
blocks.zh: 在机器人学中,这些模型充当仿真政策的几何感知编码器[32,33],视觉语言行动(VLA)模型的空间托盘提供者[34],以及SLAM和重新定位的前端[35,36]. 然而,它们几乎完全根据可容忍厘米误差的重建和本地化基准来评估。 此类模型能否交付次毫米计,闭路伺服所需的次度精度仍然开放. VGM-VS通过重新审视其几何输出作为高精度伺服的度量反馈信号来解决这一差距,以经典的IBVS[1]和特征驱动的ART-VS[5]为基准.

blocks.en: III Method
blocks.zh: 三、结 论 方法

blocks.en: In this section, we present VGM-VS, a scene-anchored visual servoing framework built on VGGT- Ω \Omega [ 11 ] and summarized in Fig. 2 . VGM-VS positions the end-effector based on the current image I I and a reference image I 0 I_{0} , captured once at the desired end-effector pose with respect to a target object. We first describe how the camera predictions of VGGT- Ω \Omega are converted into a pose increment and used for closed-loop pose-based servoing control. We then address the scale ambiguity of these predictions in two ways. Sec. III-C fits a global similarity calibration, which serves as a simple baseline, while Sec. III-D instead fine-tunes the model for metric-scale pose predictions, as adopted in VGM-VS. Finally, we introduce the automated procedure used to collect the scene-specific data on which both adaptations rely.

blocks.en: III-B Closed-Loop Pose-Based Visual Servoing
blocks.zh: 三-B 闭环式Pose-Visual Servoing

blocks.en: In principle, the predicted relative pose can be used directly to guide the robot’s motion towards the target. However the precision is the limiting factor, as it is bounded by that of a single prediction, made at an arbitrary, possibly large, distance from the target, where the object occupies only a few pixels in the image and the prediction is consequently noisier. Such a command also inherits the error of the hand–eye transform used to express it in the robot frame, and assumes a static scene throughout the motion. We therefore propose to apply this pose increment iteratively in a closed loop. Each successive iteration then moves the robot closer to the target, where predictions become gradually more accurate, analogously to a coarse-to-fine refinement, and small errors from the hand–eye calibration can also be compensated over the loop, as in IBVS [ 1 ] . Another property of VGGT- Ω \Omega is that it is explicitly trained on dynamic scenes, which further improves the robustness to disturbances such as an occlusion or a displacement of part of the scene during servoing.
blocks.zh: 原则上,预测的相对姿势可以直接用来引导机器人向目标移动. 然而精度是限制因素,因为它以单一的预测为界,在任意的,可能很大,距离目标的地方作出,物体在图像中只占据少数像素,因此预测是无名的. 这种命令还继承了用于在机器人构架中表达它的手眼变换的错误,并在整个运动中假设一个静态场景. 因此,我们建议在封闭循环中反复采用这一增加值。 每一次接连的迭代将机器人移动到更接近目标的地方,在那里预测逐渐变得更加准确,类似于粗细的精细化,手-眼校准产生的小错误也可以在环上得到补偿,如IBVS [1]. VGGT - 堆积-\Omega的另一个属性是,它被明确训练在动态场景上,这进一步提高了对扰动的稳健性,比如在伺服时对部分场景的包围或置换.

blocks.en: VGGT- Ω \Omega was not trained for the level of accuracy required by high-precision tasks, and its residual error varies with the viewpoint and the distance to the target. Rather than correcting the model’s output, we therefore let the model adapt to the scene itself.

blocks.en: We evaluate the methods on three high-precision industrial manipulation tasks: USB-C cable picking, USB-C cable insertion, and RAM insertion. The cable tasks use a Franka Emika Panda robot equipped with a Franka Hand and a wrist-mounted RealSense D405 camera. The robot grasps a cable from a holder and inserts it into a laptop USB-C port. The smooth, untextured surfaces of this scene provide too few distinctive features for ORB-IBVS and ART-VS to establish the four correspondences required by the IBVS control law, so only VGM-VS and VGM-VS w/o FT are evaluated on these two tasks. RAM insertion uses an Agile Robots Thor 3 robot equipped with a Robotiq gripper and the same wrist-mounted camera. The motherboard’s dense arrangement of electronic components provides sufficient visual features, allowing all four methods to be evaluated.

We evaluate robustness to initial-pose perturbations and scene disturbances. Initial-pose perturbations are generated relative to the camera pose at which the reference image was captured. We first apply a translational offset and orient the camera toward the target object to ensure visibility; the rotational perturbation is then applied relative to this look-at orientation. A perturbation is classified as small when its translational and rotational

Scene disturbances include occluding 25% or 50% of the target object and a dynamic setting in which the object is moved several centimeters after the reference image is captured. We conduct 100 trials for each initial-pose perturbation setting and 20 trials for each scene-disturbance setting, using the same reference image within each scene. Convergence and task-success rates are computed over all trials, while pose errors and iteration counts are averaged over converged trials.

blocks.en: IV-D Quantitative Results

blocks.en: Table I shows that VGM-VS converges in every setting of every task. The cable tasks separate the methods most sharply: the keypoint-based baselines are inapplicable there, whereas VGM-VS converges by anchoring on the target’s surroundings. On RAM insertion, where all four methods can be compared, the baselines degrade as the conditions get harder: under 50% occlusion, the convergence rates of ORB-IBVS, ART-VS, and VGM-VS w/o FT fall to 15%, 55%, and 85%. ORB-IBVS establishes more correspondences than ART-VS, which likely explains its higher convergence rate under pose perturbations, but its less distinctive features produce more outliers and a slow, oscillatory behavior costing an order of magnitude more iterations than VGM-VS: in Fig. 3 (d) and (e), the velocities of both baselines keep fluctuating along the trajectory, whereas those of VGM-VS decay smoothly to zero. ART-VS instead matches fewer points, so a few wrong ones bias the feature error and drive the camera to a wrong pose reported as converged, explaining its low iteration count and the large terminal errors in Fig. 3 (c) and (f).

VGM-VS w/o FT aligns the camera reliably in most trials, but its predictions remain inaccurate: in Fig. 3 (a) and (b) its increments overshoot and change sign before settling, unlike those of the fine-tuned model, which decay monotonically to zero. Since the loop terminates once the increment falls below τ t \tau_{t} and τ R \tau_{R} , such noise causes premature convergence several millimeters away from the target: in dynamic cable insertion, it stops after 11.6 11.6 iterations yet succeeds in none of the trials. Fine-tuning instead yields the best accuracy in every setting, with submillimeter translation and sub-degree rotation errors on both cable tasks, and drives both errors close to zero in Fig. 3 (c) and (f). blocks.en: V Conclusion
blocks.zh: 五 结论

blocks.en: In this work we have introduced VGM-VS, a scene-anchored visual servoing framework that uses a pretrained visual geometry model to estimate the relative pose between the current and the reference image, and applies it as the pose increment for a closed-loop controller. No object model, detector, or feature correspondences are needed: a single reference image defines the goal, and the surrounding workspace provides the cues when the target itself is barely visible. A short, autonomously collected robot dataset is used to fine-tune the camera head and jointly refine the hand–eye transformation, recovering metric scale and reducing the viewpoint-dependent errors that a global similarity transformation cannot correct. Adapting a new scene thus costs two minutes of recording and about two hours of training, without human intervention. Across experiments on cable picking, cable insertion, and RAM insertion, VGM-VS converged in all evaluated settings while running at 30 Hz, reaching submillimeter terminal error and sub-degree rotations on the two cable tasks, and 90–100% task success when the object is displaced during servoing, while remaining robust to texture-poor scenes, large initial displacements, and partial occlusions.
blocks.zh: 在这部作品中,我们引入了VGM-VS,一个场景-安心的视觉伺服框架,它使用预先训练的视觉几何模型来估计电流和参考图像之间的相对姿势,并将其作为闭路控制器的姿势递增. 不需要对象模型,探测器,或特征对应:一个单一的参考图像定义了目标,当目标本身几乎不可见时,周围的工作空间提供提示. 一个短而自主收集的机器人数据集被用于微调相机头,并联合完善手眼转换,恢复度量衡,减少全球相似性转换无法纠正的视线依赖错误. 因此,适应新的场景需要两分钟的录音时间和大约两小时的培训时间,而无需人类干预。 通过采电缆、电缆插入和RAM插入方面的实验,VGM-VS在运行于30赫兹时在所有评估的环境下汇合,在两个电缆任务上达到次毫米终端误差和次度旋转,当物体在伺服过程中被移动时,任务成功率达到90-100%,同时坚挺到纹理贫乏的场景、大量初始转移和部分隔离。

blocks.en: The main limitation is that the adaptation remains scene specific, as a new workspace requires another recording and training session; generalizing a single adapted model to unseen scenes is therefore an important direction for future work. Longer-horizon tasks would also require an automatic selection of the intermediate reference views, since specifying one per alignment stage by hand would introduce substantial task-specific engineering. Finally, the short contact-rich motion that completes each task is executed open loop, and integrating force feedback during this phase could further improve the task success rate.
blocks.zh: 主要的限制是,适应仍然是场景特定的,因为一个新的工作空间需要另一次录音和培训;因此,将一个经过调整的单一模型归纳到看不见的场景是未来工作的一个重要方向。 较长范围的任务还需要自动选择中间参考观点,因为单手指定一个对齐阶段将引入针对具体任务的大量工程。 最后,完成每项任务的简短的接触丰富的运动被执行开放循环,在这一阶段整合部队反馈可以进一步提高任务成功率.
